summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 20%), atrial fibrillation, obstructive sleep apnea, restrictive lung disease, and tobacco use was admitted for acute shortness of breath and orthopnea. Evaluation revealed mild interstitial edema on chest X-ray and an elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure. His symptoms were also attributed to a COPD exacerbation, given wheezing and smoking history. He was treated with increased diuresis using torsemide, a short course of prednisone, and azithromycin. His warfarin dose was temporarily reduced during antibiotic therapy. The patient was counseled on smoking cessation and provided with nicotine replacement therapy. He improved clinically, with stable oxygenation and reduced dyspnea, and was discharged home on an increased diuretic dose with instructions to monitor daily weights and follow up with his primary care and cardiology providers.
